title: BypassD: Enabling fast userspace access to shared SSDs
problem: Kernel software I/O stack introduces substantial overhead for ultra-low latency storage devices like Optane NVMe SSDs. Userspace approaches avoid this overhead but lack proper mechanisms for coordinating shared storage access without major changes to filesystems, OS, or hardware.
motivation: Modern SSDs with microsecond latencies and gigabytes-per-second bandwidth require eliminating kernel I/O stack overhead to deliver their theoretical performance.
method: BypassD enables direct userspace access to shared SSDs through coordination mechanisms that bypass the kernel I/O stack while maintaining support for concurrent storage access. The system allows multiple userspace processes to safely share SSD access without requiring modifications to filesystems, OS kernel, or underlying hardware.
key_novelty: First userspace SSD access system supporting shared storage without requiring architectural changes to filesystems, OS, or hardware.
contributions: Shared storage coordination mechanism without OS/filesystem changes
Kernel bypass I/O optimization reducing microsecond-scale latencies
Practical userspace storage access for concurrent applications

metrics.speedup: latency reduction through kernel I/O stack bypass

limitations: Limitations not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: userspace SSD access with shared storage
